scope: whole repo (src/lib/LibLeakyBucket.sol: leak, levelAt, headroomAt, fillAt, fillableAt; src/lib/LibLeakyBucketCheckpoint.sol: pack, unpack, levelAt, headroomAt, fillableAt, fill, plus the width constants and error identities; README and NatSpec as intent oracle)

summary.notes: Two rounds, looped until dry: 43 behaviours in round 1, then 6 more (error identities and the packed width constants) in round 2, which added no new gap. Round 2 ran after the round 1 coverage test landed on the branch, but every round 2 kill is credited to a pre-existing test by name, so attribution holds. Single survivor across both rounds was LibLeakyBucketCheckpoint.fillableAt, never exercised with a stored checkpoint differing from the queried clock; the one embedding test reaching it calls it in the same second as the mint, where the substitution is a no-op. Behaviour correct as written, so closed by strengthening testPackedReadsMatchCore in place plus a concrete-second case. Both adversarial findings are in the packed codec and neither is reachable through a monotonic block.timestamp: #1 is a write-path violation of the documented 'never hands out more headroom than reality' property (a timestamp behind the stored checkpoint regresses it; measured 501 units of headroom where 1 was earned, from a single zero-amount call), #2 is headroomAt/fillableAt disagreeing with fill when capacity exceeds LEAKY_BUCKET_LEVEL_MAX (fails closed, reverts on packing width rather than the documented capacity error). publishedTag is null: nothing is published yet, the next-v0.1.0 tag is an unconsumed version seed and the Soldeer project does not exist. testsAfterCommit is the coverage commit on branch mutation-test/leaky-bucket, pending merge of PR #3.

summary.notes: Maintenance re-probe, not a discovery scan: the previous record described 6398377 and the merges invalidated it, which is what mutation-scan-freshness was failing on (and, through the publish gate's refusal to release a commit with a failed run, what was failing Package Release on main). Eleven of the 59 prior mutants were HARNESS-ERROR against the merged tree because the refactors moved their targets (M08-M11 and M19 through the headroomFrom extraction, M41 through fillableAt binding its result before the sentinel clamp, M48/M49 through the width constants becoming derived, M57-M59 through checkCapacity becoming checkFillableDomain); all eleven were retargeted to the current source with their intent preserved, and M11 and M57-M59 renamed where the refactor changed what the mutation now means. Eighteen new mutants (M60-M77) cover the behaviour that landed after 6398377 and had nothing targeting it. Result: 77/77 killed, 0 survived, 0 no-run, 0 harness errors, on a green 80-test baseline. Every one of the 18 new mutants was killed by the PRE-EXISTING suite, so this run added no tests and testsAfterCommit equals the scanned commit. Adversarial pass over the new behaviour raised no candidate: leakRatePer's floor division matches its documented 'rounds DOWN so the on chain rate is never faster than the policy', its shortfall is under one unit a second as claimed, and its zero-period panic is documented intent rather than an unhandled input.

scope: re-probe after pack's two overflow guards were restored, superseding the entry above it in this file. Four mutants added for the restored guards (M54-M57), 57 total, all against src/lib/LibLeakyBucket.sol.

summary.notes: THREE SURVIVORS, recorded rather than removed, and they are a finding rather than a gap in the tests. M55 (level guard never fires), M56 (level guard raises the capacity error) and M57 (timestamp packed unchecked) all survive because pack's REJECTION paths cannot be reached through fill, which is its only caller and which bounds both fields first: checkFillableDomain refuses a capacity above LEAKY_BUCKET_LEVEL_MAX and a timestamp above LEAKY_BUCKET_TIMESTAMP_MAX, unpack can only produce a level and a checkpoint already inside their fields, and fillAt returns at most the larger of that level and the capacity. No test can reach them without exposing pack, which would add the surface this release exists to remove. M54, the off-by-one that would reject a legitimate capacity exactly at LEAKY_BUCKET_LEVEL_MAX, IS killed, so the guard's boundary is exercised even though its rejection is not. The adversarial question was asked of all three: the current behaviour is correct, the guards are simply unreachable today. They are kept deliberately as defence against a future second caller, a decision made by the repository owner after this redundancy was measured. This entry is the evidence for that redundancy and replaces the prose argument that previously sat in pack's NatSpec, which was removed for asserting a property of the call graph that nothing enforces.

scope: re-probe after a comment-only edit to src/lib/LibLeakyBucket.sol (#108). No executable code changed; the mutants and their targets are identical to the entry above.

summary.notes: Verdicts identical to the previous entry, as expected: the only change was three lines of NatSpec. Recorded because check-scan-freshness.sh diffs the src/ and test/ trees byte for byte and cannot tell a comment from a statement, so a documentation fix inside src/ costs a full 57-mutant probe to earn the record back. That is the gate behaving correctly rather than a defect - a check that tried to distinguish comments from code would be a check that could be fooled. Survivors are unchanged and unchanged in reason: M55, M56 and M57 are pack's rejection paths, which fill bounds out of reach before pack is called. M54, the off-by-one that would refuse a legitimate capacity at LEAKY_BUCKET_LEVEL_MAX, is killed.
